newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open sharply higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open up sharply Friday in line with LME copper which climbed to its highest level in 10 weeks in London after a further large drawdown in warehouse stocks.
COMEX December copper was called up 2.00 to 3.00 cents from Thursday's close of 95.85 cents a lb. It traded as high as 100.15 cents on ACCESS.
LME copper warehouse stocks fell 8,000 tonnes to 101,175 tonnes Friday, a six-year low, while COMEX copper stocks rose 376 short tons to 32,750 short tons Thursday.
COMEX December copper has been recovering erratically from a low of 82.80 cents set in June. It scaled a five-month peak earlier this week of 98.80 cents.

But Wednesday, LME copper and COMEX copper corrected downward after World Bureau of Metal Statistics said in a monthly report there could be 500,000 tonnes of copper in unbonded warehouses in Rotterdam.
